title: Lefthook configuration
markdownDescription:
Configuration for Lefthook, a fast and powerful Git hooks manager.

Lefthook allows you to manage Git hooks with a simple YAML/JSON/TOML configuration file. It supports running commands in parallel, filtering files by glob patterns, and much more.

[Lefthook Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/)

hook.markdownDescription:
Configuration for a specific Git hook (e.g., pre-commit, pre-push).

Defines commands and scripts to run when the hook is triggered. You can configure parallel execution, file filtering, and conditional execution.

[Hook Configuration Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/Hook/)

files.markdownDescription: A custom git command for files to be referenced in {files} template.

piped.markdownDescription: Stop running commands and scripts if one of them fail.

follow.markdownDescription: Follow the STDOUT of the running commands and scripts.

fail_on_changes.markdownDescription:
Whether lefthook should exit with a non-zero status if files tracked by git were modified while running the hook.

- `never` (default): never fail on changes
- `always`: always fail on changes
- `ci`: fail only when the `CI` environment variable is set
- `non-ci`: fail only when the `CI` environment variable is _not_ set

[Docs](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/fail_on_changes/)

fail_on_changes_diff.markdownDescription:
Whether to print a diff of the detected changes when `fail_on_changes` triggers. By default the diff is printed only in CI.

[Docs](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/fail_on_changes_diff/)

setup.markdownDescription:
A list of instructions to run before any job. Supports templates and Git args like in `run`.

When merging configs, `setup` instructions get prepended.

[Docs](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/setup/)

run.markdownDescription: Shell command to execute before any job.

exclude_tags.markdownDescription: Tags or command names that you want to exclude. This option can be overwritten with `LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE` env variable.

jobs.markdownDescription:
List of jobs to execute for this hook.

Jobs provide more flexibility than commands by allowing you to nest groups, define dependencies, and control execution order.

[Jobs Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/jobs/)

commands.markdownDescription:
Named commands to execute for this hook.

Each property name represents a command identifier, and its value defines the command configuration.

Example:
```yaml
commands:
  lint:
    run: eslint {staged_files}
```

[Commands Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/Commands/)

scripts.markdownDescription:
Named scripts to execute for this hook.

Scripts are executable files stored in `.lefthook/` or `.lefthook-local/` directories. Each property name should match a script filename.

[Scripts Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/Scripts/)

condition.markdownDescription:
Condition for skipping or only running commands/scripts.

Can be a simple string (`rebase`, `merge`, `merge-commit`) or, inside a list, an object with `ref` (branch pattern) or `run` (shell command to determine condition).

[Skip/Only Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/skip/)

ref.markdownDescription:
Git branch pattern to match (supports globs).

Example: `"main"` or `"feature/*"`

run.markdownDescription:
Shell command to determine if condition is met.

Command should exit with status 0 for true, non-zero for false.

Example: `"test -f .env"`

job.markdownDescription:
A job defines a unit of work to execute within a hook.

Jobs can run commands, execute scripts, or group other jobs together. They support file filtering, conditional execution, and environment variables.

[Jobs Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/jobs/)

name.markdownDescription: Name of a job. Will be printed in summary. If specified, the jobs can be merged with a jobs of the same name in a local config or extends.

run.markdownDescription:
Shell command to execute.

Supports templates like `{staged_files}`, `{all_files}`, `{files}`, `{cmd}`, etc.

Example: `"eslint {staged_files}"`

[Run Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/run/)

script.markdownDescription:
Script filename to execute (relative to `.lefthook/` or `.lefthook-local/`).

Example: `"lint.sh"`

[Scripts Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/Scripts/)

runner.markdownDescription:
Custom command to run the script or job.

Example: `"docker run -it --rm <container> {cmd}"`

[Runner Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/runner/)

group.markdownDescription:
Group of jobs to execute together with shared configuration.

If `env`, `root`, `glob`, `exclude`, or `files` are set on the job containing the group, they are inherited by the nested jobs.

[Group Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/group/)

parallel.markdownDescription:
Run jobs in this group concurrently.

Default: `false`

piped.markdownDescription:
Stop running jobs if one of them fails.

Default: `false`

command.markdownDescription:
A named command configuration.

Commands are simpler than jobs but offer most of the same features. Use commands when you don't need job grouping or complex dependencies.

[Commands Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/Commands/)

priority.markdownDescription:
This option makes sense only when parallel: false or piped: true is set.

Value 0 is considered an +Infinity, so commands or scripts with priority: 0 or without this setting will be run at the very end.

script.markdownDescription:
A script file configuration.

Scripts are executable files stored in `.lefthook/` or `.lefthook-local/` directories. Scripts are simpler than commands – they don't support file filtering directly but can use environment variables.

[Scripts Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/Scripts/)

priority.markdownDescription:
This option makes sense only when parallel: false or piped: true is set.

Value 0 is considered an +Infinity, so commands or scripts with priority: 0 or without this setting will be run at the very end.

env.markdownDescription:
Environment variables to set for the command/script.

Example:
```yaml
env:
  NODE_ENV: production
  DEBUG: "true"
```

[Env Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/env/)

tags.markdownDescription:
Tags to categorize commands/scripts.

Use `exclude_tags` in hooks to skip commands with certain tags. Useful for organizing frontend/backend, security/linting, etc.

[Tags Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/tags/)

color.markdownDescription: An ANSI color code (e.g. `14`) or a hex color (e.g. `"#32CD32"`).

args.markdownDescription:
Arguments appended to the command or script. Supports the same templates as `run`.

Arguments passed by Git are omitted if `args` is specified. Providing no `args` is the same as `args: "{0}"`.

[Args Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/args/)

timeout.markdownDescription: Maximum time the job is allowed to run, as a Go duration string (e.g. `15s`, `1m30s`).

glob.markdownDescription:
Glob pattern(s) to filter files.

Only commands will run if matching files exist. Supports glob syntax like `**/*.js`, `*.{ts,tsx}`, etc.

[Glob Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/glob/)

files.markdownDescription: A custom git command for files or directories to be referenced in {files} template for run setting.

file_type.markdownDescription:
File type filter.

Filter files by type before passing to commands.

[File Types Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/file_types/)

exclude.markdownDescription:
A list of globs to be excluded.

[Exclude Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/exclude/)

skip.markdownDescription: You can skip all or specific commands and scripts using the `skip` option. You can also skip when merging, rebasing, or being on a specific branch. Globs are available for branches.

only.markdownDescription: You can force a command, script, or the whole hook to execute only in certain conditions. This option acts like the opposite of `skip`. It accepts the same values but skips execution only if the condition is _not_ satisfied.

$schema.markdownDescription: The JSON schema for this configuration file.

ai.markdownDescription:
**Beta.** LLM agent hook integration. Each key is a provider name whose value maps the provider's event names to lefthook hook names defined in this config. During `lefthook install` the provider-specific settings file is generated so the agent calls `lefthook run <hook>` when the event fires.

Example:
```yaml
ai:
  claude:
    Stop: validate
```

[AI Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/ai/)

claude.markdownDescription: Claude Code hook mappings (event name -> lefthook hook name). Generates `.claude/settings.json`.

codex.markdownDescription: Codex CLI hook mappings (event name -> lefthook hook name). Generates `.codex/hooks.json`.

cursor.markdownDescription: Cursor hook mappings (event name -> lefthook hook name). Generates `.cursor/hooks.json`.

copilot.markdownDescription: GitHub Copilot hook mappings (event name -> lefthook hook name). Generates `.github/hooks/lefthook.json`.

assert_lefthook_installed.markdownDescription: When set to `true`, fail (with exit status 1) if lefthook executable can't be found in $PATH, under node_modules/, as a Ruby gem, or other supported method. This makes sure git hook won't omit lefthook rules if lefthook ever was installed.

colors.markdownDescription:
Whether to enable colorful output. With the default `auto`, colors are enabled only when a color capable terminal is detected; `on` (or `true`) forces colors, `off` (or `false`) disables them. You can also provide your own color codes.

[Colors Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/colors/)

anyOf.markdownDescription:
Custom color configuration using ANSI codes or hex colors.

Example:
```yaml
colors:
  cyan: 14
  gray: 244
  green: "#00FF00"
```

[Colors Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/colors/)

extends.markdownDescription:
List of configuration files to extend/merge.

Allows you to compose configuration from multiple files. Paths can be globs (e.g. `projects/*/lefthook.yml`).

Example: `["lefthook-base.yml", "lefthook-team.yml"]`

[Extends Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/extends/)

glob_matcher.markdownDescription:
Glob matching engine used for `glob` and `exclude` patterns.

- `gobwas` (default): `**/*.js` matches `src/app.js` but not `app.js`
- `doublestar`: standard (Bash-like) behavior, `**/*.js` matches files at any depth including the root

[Glob Matcher Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/glob_matcher/)

install_non_git_hooks.markdownDescription:
Install non-Git hooks (hooks with names that aren't Git hooks) into `.git/hooks`. May be useful with tools like git-flow.

[Docs](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/install_non_git_hooks/)

lefthook.markdownDescription: Provide a full path to lefthook executable or a command to run lefthook. Bourne shell (`sh`) syntax is supported.

min_version.markdownDescription:
Minimum required Lefthook version.

If the installed version is lower, Lefthook will fail with an error.

Example: `"1.5.0"`

[Min Version Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/min_version/)

no_auto_install.markdownDescription:
Disable automatic installation and synchronization of git hooks when running `lefthook run`. Can also be set with the `--no-auto-install` option.

[Docs](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/no_auto_install/)

no_tty.markdownDescription: Whether hide spinner and other interactive things.

output.markdownDescription:
Control what Lefthook outputs to the console.

Can be set to `false` to print only errors, or a list (or comma-separated string) of output types to show. By default all output is enabled.

Available types: `meta`, `summary`, `empty_summary`, `success`, `failure`, `execution`, `execution_out`, `execution_info`, `skips`, `setup`

Can be overridden with the `LEFTHOOK_OUTPUT` environment variable.

[Output Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/output/)

rc.markdownDescription:
Path to a shell script that will be sourced before running hooks.

Useful for setting up environment variables or loading shell functions.

Example: `".lefthookrc"`

[RC Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/rc/)

remotes.markdownDescription:
List of remote Git repositories containing shared Lefthook configurations.

Allows teams to share and reuse hook configurations across multiple projects.

[Remotes Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/remotes/)

git_url.markdownDescription: A URL to Git repository. It will be accessed with privileges of the machine lefthook runs on.

ref.markdownDescription: An optional branch or tag name.

refetch.markdownDescription: Force remote config refetching on every run. Lefthook will be refetching the specified remote every time it is called.

refetch_frequency.markdownDescription: Specifies how frequently Lefthook should refetch the remote configuration. This can be set to always, never or a time duration like 24h, 30m, etc.

configs.markdownDescription:
Array of config file paths from the remote repository's root.

Example: `["lefthook.yml", "configs/pre-commit.yml"]`

[Configs Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/configs/)

source_dir.markdownDescription:
Change a directory for script files. Directory for script files contains folders with git hook names which contain script files.

[Docs](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/source_dir/)

source_dir_local.markdownDescription: Change a directory for _local_ script files (not stored in VCS).

skip_lfs.markdownDescription: Skip running LFS hooks even if it exists on your system.

templates.markdownDescription:
Custom template replacements for `{template_name}` placeholders in `run` commands.

Example:
```yaml
templates:
  wrapper: docker compose run --rm app
```

Then use in commands: `run: "{wrapper} npm test"`

[Templates Documentation](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/templates/)

pre-commit.markdownDescription:
Git pre-commit hook configuration.

Runs before `git commit` is finalized. Commonly used for linting, formatting, and running tests on staged files.

[Pre-commit Hook](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/Hook/)

pre-push.markdownDescription:
Git pre-push hook configuration.

Runs before `git push`. Commonly used for running full test suites, security audits, or build verification.

[Pre-push Hook](https://lefthook.dev/configuration/Hook/)
